chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of: from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū al-Qāsim and Abū Qatādah, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar. And he also informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAmrakī ibn ʿAlī al-Naysābūrī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar. And he also informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAmrakī ibn ʿAlī al-Naysābūrī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a wet mouse that had fallen into water, then walked on clothes: may one pray in them? He said: “Wash what you see of its trace, and what you do not see, sprinkle it with water.” And in the narration of Abū Qatādah from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar: “And the dog is like that.”

The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: Likewise, if one of the things we mentioned touches the human body, or his hand falls upon it while it is wet, he should wash whatever it affected of him; and if it is dry, he should wipe it with dust. What has preceded already contains that which indicates this and further clarifies it.

key_terms.أَثَرِهَا: its trace, meaning the visible sign of contact or impurity
key_terms.اغْسِلْ: wash, indicating removal of visible impurity with water
key_terms.الثِّيَابِ: clothes or garments upon which the impurity may have spread
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse, discussed here as a source of najasah contamination
key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: the dog, stated here to have the same ruling in this context
key_terms.بِالتُّرَابِ: with dust, mentioned in the Shaykh’s statement regarding dry contact
key_terms.رَطْبًا: wet, a condition affecting transfer of impurity
key_terms.فَانْضَحْهُ: sprinkle it, referring to applying water where no visible trace is seen

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a wet mouse or dog touches clothing or the body before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on clothing contacted by a wet mouse, stating that visible traces are to be washed and unseen areas are to be sprinkled with water. It also extends the same ruling to the dog in one narration, and the Shaykh adds a related ruling regarding contact with the human body in cases of wetness and dryness.
